analysis.analysis_scope: 12 most recently added KEVs; counts cover those KEVs only. Up to 3 HTML detail items per enabled advisory index, sorted by published date when available.

priority_method.Critical: Known exploitation plus code/command execution or authentication bypass and an explicit unauthenticated, remote, root, administrator, or ransomware consequence in the record.
priority_method.High: Known exploitation plus code/command execution, authentication bypass, privilege escalation, sensitive-data exposure, spoofing, or recorded ransomware use.
priority_method.Anomaly: Non-CVE advisory or campaign retained for monitoring; not a vendor severity score.
priority_method.Medium: Known exploitation without the higher-priority lexical signals; validate asset exposure and business impact. Never implies safe to ignore.
priority_method.Low: Reserved; not assigned to KEV entries because catalog inclusion establishes exploitation.

ics_advisories.title: Siemens Desigo, Gridscale
ics_advisories.summary: On October 21, 2026, the Node.js project released security updates addressing a critical vulnerability in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, commonly referred to as "Node2Shell" (tracked as CVE-2026-111497). The vulnerability is an out-of-bounds write that could allow a remote attacker to cause memory corruption and potentially execute arbitrary code. This advisory covers the status of impact of various Siemens software products. Siemens has released new versions for the affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions.
ics_advisories.priority_rationale: Advisory text signals only; this does not assert KEV inclusion or active exploitation. Textual impact plus code/command execution or authentication bypass and an explicit unauthenticated, remote, root, administrator, or ransomware consequence in the record.

official_ic3_items.title: Suspicious Letters Containing White Powder Mailed to State and Local Election Officials, Media Organizations, and Public and Private Polling Companies
official_ic3_items.summary: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and the U.S. Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) are investigating multiple letters containing suspicious substances mailed to various locations nationwide, including elected officials, Secretaries of State and their related election offices, and various election-related entities. Law enforcement is working diligently to intercept any additional letters before they are delivered. To date, no hazardous material has been identified; however, laboratory testing remains ongoing. All suspicious substances should be treated as hazardous and must be handled in accordance with established safety protocols.
official_ic3_items.priority_rationale: Non-CVE official advisory: monitoring label, not evidence of a vulnerability severity or confirmed exploitation.

official_ic3_items.title: Critical Vulnerability Alert: PHP Core
official_ic3_items.summary: In a follow on to the FBI's initial social media posting on October 21st regarding the identified PHP vulnerabilities, the FBI is sharing this PSA to continue to warn the public of the criticality and necessity to take steps to protect any affected networks from these known vulnerabilities. PHP is a widely used programming language that powers websites and web applications. These vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) could allow malicious cyber actors to remotely execute code in PHP core, potentially compromising sensitive data and networks.

official_ic3_items.title: Cyber Threat Actors Use a Variety of Techniques to Target Election and Campaign Officials
official_ic3_items.summary: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) are providing this Public Service Announcement (PSA) to raise awareness of the cyber threats facing election and campaign officials during the upcoming 2026 U.S. midterm elections. Additionally, this announcement provides the public with information on techniques, including phishing1 and smishing2, that malicious cyber actors have used during past election cycles.
